solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: A variable in diagram minus one — is square (5)

indicatorNotes.in: A Z goes inside what is left of the diagram
indicatorNotes.minus one: the diagram loses one letter, its last

blocks.note: a plan is a diagram, as of a building
PLAN drops one letter, its final N
A, plus Z, a letter standing for an unknown in algebra

annotation.surface: A maths lesson: a variable is placed in a diagram, one taken away, and the result is squared.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash and 'is square' make it read as algebra, but square is the definition, a town square, and 'variable' is the usual crossword signal for X, Y or Z.
annotation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town.

entries.clue: King feeding another man peach snack (5,7)

indicatorNotes.feeding: the king is fed into the other man, going inside him

blocks.note: a pawn is a chessman, 'another' after the king
a cracker, like a peach, is an excellent specimen

annotation.surface: A king is served a peach as a snack by one of his men.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece: the king is one, so 'another man' is the pawn. Peach and cracker are both British slang for something first-rate. A prawn cracker is a puffy fried snack from Chinese takeaways.
annotation.definitionFit: A prawn cracker is a light, crisp fried snack.

entries.clue: Old buffoon critical of Conservative (5)

annotation.surface: A former clown who disapproves of the Conservative party.
annotation.walkthrough: Antic is now usually an adjective or 'antics', but in Shakespeare's day an antic was a grotesque clown, hence 'Old'.
annotation.definitionFit: Antic is an archaic noun for a buffoon or grotesque performer.

entries.clue: Very much the negotiator’s aim? (1,4,4)

blocks.note: an adverbial phrase of quantity, as in '___ better'
what someone bargaining hopes to walk away with

annotation.surface: An emphatic reply confirming what someone bargaining is after.
annotation.walkthrough: The same phrase does two jobs: an adverb of quantity, and a favourable bargain. The question mark admits the second is a bit of fun.
annotation.definitionFit: 'A good deal' means very much, as in 'a good deal older'.

entries.clue: Fish: list ten before the queen then? (8)

annotation.definition2: list ten before the queen then?

blocks.note: a kind of tuna, named for leaping from the water

blocks.clueFragment: list ten before the queen then?
blocks.note: counting up the cards, ten, jack, queen: going straight from ten to queen means you skip the jack

annotation.surface: A card-player's puzzle about the order of ten and queen, with a fish attached.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the second half as an instruction: in card order the jack sits between ten and queen, so listing ten and then the queen is to SKIP JACK.
annotation.definitionFit: The skipjack tuna is a common food fish.

entries.clue: Mac she used in reordering synopsis (6)

indicatorNotes.reordering: the letters of MAC SHE are put in a new order

annotation.surface: Someone used a Mac computer to rework a summary.
annotation.walkthrough: Mac looks like the Apple computer, which makes 'reordering' sound like editing a document.
annotation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or summary plan of something.

entries.clue: Forcefully demanded I crushed dissent (8)

indicatorNotes.crushed: the letters of DISSENT are broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: An authority figure boasting of having put down opposition.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a strongman's boast, and the definition sits in the same voice: crushing dissent is exactly what an insistent ruler does.
annotation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand something forcefully.

entries.clue: Patriarch embraces Rebecca and Isaac ultimately — their son? (5)

indicatorNotes.embraces: the patriarch's name wraps round the two letters
indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of each name

blocks.note: Job, the Old Testament figure, counted among the patriarchs
last letters of RebeccA and IsaaC

annotation.surface: A biblical family tree: a patriarch, Rebecca and Isaac, and the question of their son.
annotation.walkthrough: Rebecca and Isaac really were Jacob's parents, so the definition comes straight from the story the surface tells.
annotation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob is the son of Isaac and Rebecca.

entries.clue: Country’s top player first of all in cup appearance (5,4)

indicatorNotes.first of all: take the first letter of every word that follows

blocks.note: first letters of In Cup Appearance

annotation.surface: A nation's star footballer making his first appearance in a cup match.
annotation.walkthrough: The football picture hides that 'first of all' applies to all three following words, not just 'in'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Central American republic is one country among many.

entries.clue: Star student, when is first in theory, receives prize like that (14)

indicatorNotes.receives: AS...IST takes the prize and SIC inside it

blocks.note: as = when, as in 'as I left'
sic, Latin 'thus', marks a quotation as written like that

annotation.surface: A top pupil who, when theory comes first, wins an award for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Star student' reads as a brilliant pupil but means someone who studies stars. AS + IST opens up to hold TROPHY + SIC.
annotation.definitionFit: An astrophysicist studies the physics of stars.

entries.clue: Winger dodges argument about expected score (5,7)

blocks.note: to hedge is to dodge a direct answer
par is the expected score on a golf hole
a row (rhymes with 'cow') is a quarrel

annotation.surface: A footballer on the wing avoids a dispute over what the scoreline should have been.
annotation.walkthrough: Winger reads as a wide footballer but means anything with wings. An argument about par is a PAR ROW, the topic named first.
annotation.definitionFit: The hedge sparrow, or dunnock, is a small bird.

entries.clue: Biblical character consumed, I gathered (9)

indicatorNotes.gathered: the letters are collected up and rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone reporting what they had understood a Bible figure had eaten.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I gathered' reads as 'I understood', hiding that 'gathered' is the instruction and I is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Nicodemus is the Pharisee who visits Jesus by night in John's Gospel.

entries.clue: Valorous British party (5)

annotation.surface: A courageous British political party.
annotation.walkthrough: Party suggests politics after 'British', but here it is a dance party.
annotation.definitionFit: Brave and valorous both mean courageous.

entries.clue: Pulse in competitor? (6)

blocks.note: pulses are edible seeds such as beans; a climbing bean grown in British gardens
someone who runs in a race

annotation.surface: A heartbeat inside an athlete.
annotation.walkthrough: Pulse means a heartbeat on the surface but an edible seed here: the runner bean is a common British garden vegetable.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain: the runner bean is a legume, so a pulse, and anyone running a race competes.

entries.clue: Deputy feeling less outspoken as well (6,3)

indicatorNotes.outspoken: spoken out, so the word is given by its sound

annotation.surface: A second-in-command who has grown numb and is also blunt.
annotation.walkthrough: NUMBER here is the comparative of numb, pronounced without the B, not the counting word.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from ranking: whoever comes second in command after the boss is the deputy.

entries.clue: Starting to feel appropriate (8)

blocks.note: growing to be, as in '___ tired'

annotation.surface: Beginning to sense that something is right.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses are unrelated: 'becoming anxious' and 'a becoming modesty'.
annotation.definitionFit: Becoming means growing to be, and also suitable or fitting.

entries.clue: Surreptitiously hide notes all over the place (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.all over the place: the letters are scattered into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone secretly stashing messages in every corner.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's secrecy matches the definition, which keeps the reader thinking about hiding rather than rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something on the side means doing it secretly, beyond one's official role.

entries.clue: Show peg pinning casual garment (8)

indicatorNotes.pinning: the peg holds the garment inside it

blocks.note: a golf tee is a peg

annotation.surface: A clothes peg holding up a pair of jeans on display.
annotation.walkthrough: Peg and pinning suggest a washing line; the peg is the golfer's tee.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the broadcasting sense: to put something on air is to show it.

entries.clue: African driver’s ruckus while being driven? (8)

indicatorNotes.while being: the ruckus happens within the vehicle that is driven

blocks.note: a car is what gets driven
a melee is a confused fight

annotation.surface: A chauffeur in Africa causing a commotion while at the wheel.
annotation.walkthrough: A punch-up while being driven happens inside the vehicle. The driver is not a motorist but someone who drives camels.
annotation.definitionFit: A cameleer drives camels, as in North Africa.

entries.clue: Crew on board ship cooks (6)

indicatorNotes.on board: goes inside SS, the steamship's abbreviation

annotation.surface: Sailors working the galley on a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' looks like a noun, the ship's cooks, but is a verb, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To steam is to cook with vapour; 'steams' and 'cooks' are both verbs.

entries.clue: Head going mad over inspection’s conclusion (6)

indicatorNotes.mad: the letters of GOING go crazy and rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone losing their mind over the end of an inspection.
annotation.walkthrough: Head is the definition, not a head teacher panicking about an inspection. The N joins GOING as extra fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Noggin is informal British slang for the head.

entries.clue: Finally free, so all possible (5)

annotation.surface: At last released, so anything can happen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All possible' works as in 'every chance of success', meaning the fullest possible amount.
annotation.definitionFit: Every can mean all possible, as in 'given every opportunity'.

entries.clue: Boat last to employ crew from Germany? (5)

blocks.note: an eight is a rowing crew; eight in German is acht

annotation.surface: A boat that was the last to hire German sailors.
annotation.walkthrough: The crew is a rowing eight, and the question mark flags that you must then translate it into German.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the yacht is a sailing or motor vessel kept for pleasure or racing, a kind of boat.

entries.clue: Arcane things I create, so cryptic (9)

indicatorNotes.cryptic: the letters are made obscure, jumbled

annotation.surface: A crossword setter explaining why their work is so puzzling.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter seems to describe their own crosswords, and 'cryptic' is both the joke and the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure things understood by few.

entries.clue: I managed to grab sunbed in the end — and took it easy (5)

indicatorNotes.to grab: I LED holds the letter inside

annotation.surface: A holidaymaker who got a sunbed by the pool and then lazed.
annotation.walkthrough: The poolside scene fits the definition so well that 'sunbed' seems to be the point; only its last letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lazing about without working is taking it easy, both in the past tense.

entries.clue: Present member’s role? (8,6)

blocks.note: a member is a limb, and a leg's job is to fill a stocking

annotation.surface: A question about what part someone in an organisation currently plays.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member' reads as a club member but means a limb: a leg fills a stocking.
annotation.definitionFit: A stocking filler is a small gift put in a Christmas stocking.

entries.clue: Polar bear’s back, on returning with particular force? (8)

indicatorNotes.back: the back of a word is its end, so take the last letter of 'bear'
indicatorNotes.returning: coming back the way it went, so R ON is read right to left

blocks.note: ON as written; R ON then turns round
the definite article singles out a particular one
RN = Royal Navy, an armed force

annotation.surface: A polar bear turning round with great strength.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Polar bear' is split: Polar is the definition and bear only gives its last letter. Force means an armed service here, not a push.
annotation.definitionFit: Polar means relating to the poles, and the North Pole is northern.

entries.clue: Object that’s sensitive gift (5)

blocks.note: an end is an aim or object
'ow!' is what you say when something is sensitive and hurts

annotation.surface: A present that is a delicate, touchy item.
annotation.walkthrough: Gift reads as a noun but is the verb, to give; object also means aim, not a thing.
annotation.definitionFit: Gift is used as a verb, a plain synonym for bestowing money or a quality on someone.
